Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.lang

Class Ast

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.lang.Ast
public final class Ast extends Object
The Mandela abstract syntax tree.

The tree is a set of immutable records in one file, grouped as expressions, statements and patterns. Every node carries its 1-based source position, so a compile error or an editor outline can point at the exact token without a side table, and Ast.Walk gives hosts (the editor's Structure panel, the linter) a visitor that needs no instanceof chain outside this file.

Design points a reader should know before changing the grammar:

  • Desugaring happens here, not in the VM. The parser turns a |> f(x) into f(a, x) and fun f(x) = expr into a function whose body returns expr, so the compiler only ever sees one canonical shape. Sugar that changes evaluation order must not be desugared this way; the pipe's left operand is evaluated exactly once, which the rewritten call preserves.
  • No expression statements ambiguity. An expression used as a statement is wrapped in Ast.Stmt.Expression, so the compiler knows to drop its value.
  • Types are declarations, not annotations. Mandela is dynamically typed; Ast.Stmt.TypeDecl, Ast.Stmt.ClassDecl and Ast.Stmt.EnumDecl create runtime values, while : Int in a parameter list is an optional, unchecked documentation hint carried by Ast.Param.typeName for editors and tooling.
